mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in a month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in a single month
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during FEDFUNDS > 4.0% months, or the IC > 0.05 with a t-stat < 1.96.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2% in a month, it predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate future inflation normalization and rate cuts.
failure_condition: Across 3 consecutive months with CPIAUCSL > +2% change, 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a baseline (IC > 0.10, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (labor market additions) accompanied by a decline in UNRATE (unemployment) signals a tight labor market, which precedes a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as firms expand hiring and confidence rises.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month AND UNRATE falls by >0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: During 10 such labor market tightening events, the 5-day forward return mean is not significantly higher than zero (IC > 0.15, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in INDPRO (industrial production) below 100 suggests weakening manufacturing momentum, which predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors reassess growth prospects.
failure_condition: Over 5 such softening episodes, the 20-day forward return mean is not negative (IC < -0.10, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (home sales) falls by more than 5% in a month, it indicates cooling housing demand, which precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as equities adjust to slower economic activity.
failure_condition: During 4 such events, the 60-day forward return mean is not negative (IC > -0.10, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in GDPC1 (real GDP) accompanied by FEDFUNDS < 1.00% suggests a recessionary environment, which is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 3-month cumulative decline AND FEDFUNDS < 1.00% for the same period
failure_condition: During 3 such recessionary dual signals, the 20-day forward return mean is not negative (IC > 0.05, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in RSAFS (retail sales) above 1.5% month-over-month in a month coinciding with UNRATE < 4.0% suggests consumer confidence and labor market slack, both of which predict a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
regime_hint: Labor market slack and retail strength
failure_condition: Across 8 such events, the 5-day forward return mean is not significantly positive (IC < 0.10, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE remains above 5% for two consecutive months and INDPRO is flat (< 0.5% change), it signals weak labor demand and muted industrial activity, which precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% for two consecutive months AND INDPRO monthly change <= 0.5%
regime_hint: Labor market slack and flat production
failure_condition: During 6 such episodes, the 60-day forward return mean is not negative (IC > -0.10, p > 0.05).
